ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the linear function $y_1=kx+b$ intersects with the x-axis at point $A$ and with the y-axis at point $B$. It intersects with the graph of the inverse proportion function $y_2=\frac{m}{x}$ at points $C$ and $D$, where point $C(-2,3)$, and the ordinate of point $D$ is $-1$. Find the analytic expressions of the inverse proportion function and the linear function?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the inverse proportional function $y_2=\frac{m}{x}$ passes through point $C(-2, 3)$, substituting gives:\\
$\therefore m=-2\times 3=-6$,\\
$\therefore$ the equation of the inverse proportional function is $y=-\frac{6}{x}$;\\
Given the y-coordinate of point $D$ is $-1$,\\
$\therefore D(6, -1)$,\\
Substituting points $C$ and $D$ into $y_1=kx+b$,\\
we get $\begin{cases}-2k+b=3\\ 6k+b=-1\end{cases}$, solving this gives $\begin{cases}k=-\frac{1}{2}\\ b=2\end{cases}$,\\
$\therefore$ the equation of the inverse proportional function is $\boxed{y=-\frac{6}{x}}$,\\
$\therefore$ the equation of the linear function is $\boxed{y=-\frac{1}{2}x+2}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a rectangular coordinate system; a straight line slanting from the upper left to the lower right intersects the x-axis at A and intersects the y-axis at B; the two branches of the hyperbola are located in the second quadrant and the fourth quadrant respectively; the straight line and the hyperbola have two intersection points, the upper-left one is labeled C, and the lower-right one is labeled D. The problem gives C=(-2,3), and the ordinate of point D is -1. Reasoning: According to the meaning of the problem, C and D are both common points of the straight line y1=kx+b and the inverse proportional function y2=m/x. Because C=(-2,3) is on the inverse proportional function y=m/x, m=xy=(-2)*3=-6, therefore the inverse proportional function is y=-6/x. Also because D is also on this hyperbola and y_D=-1, substitute -1=-6/x_D to obtain x_D=6, so D=(6,-1). Substitute C and D into the straight line y=kx+b to get -2k+b=3 and 6k+b=-1. Subtracting the two equations gives 8k=-4, so k=-1/2; then substitute into 6k+b=-1 to get -3+b=-1, so b=2. Therefore the straight line is y=-1/2 x+2.
